reason: Runnable (pure python ints as F_2[t], weak Popov, dims 9/25/49, a few CPU-min) and the metric is structural (row degrees vs determinant degree), good. But as written it does not discriminate. (1) Grid vs thresholds: I computed the box-shift average-degree thresholds avg(s)/avg(a+b) for k=1..8: 0.0556, 0.1, 0.1190, 0.1296, 0.1364, 0.1410, 0.1444, 0.1471 (1/18, 1/10, 0.119 confirmed; limit 1/6 only as k->inf). The smallest nonzero grid point l/n=1/8=0.125 exceeds the k=1,2,3 thresholds, so with k<=3 every cell is predicted FAIL: the true-arm prediction is all-zero, indistinguishable from a broken reducer; the 'never above 1/6' and 'zero at >=1/4' predictions are vacuous at k<=3. Grid also has integer-l granularity (n=31, 1/6 -> l=5). (2) Near-tautology: the lattice does not depend on the planted root (determinant is root-independent), and exact weak-Popov reduction makes sum of row degrees = det degree an identity; 'success' degree<kn is arithmetic, not a test of the Coppersmith claim. The only empirical content is whether the 2nd-shortest row (needed for a bivariate root: >=2 coprime polys) is also below kn, since the average-degree count guarantees only 1 vector, and whether S_3's char-2 structure (square part Q^2 + X1X2X3 + a6, x1<->x2 symmetry) yields extra short vectors beyond a generic bidegree-(2,2) polynomial. The prediction does not state the 2-vector threshold and has no generic-polynomial null. (3) Null/control: univariate 'exactly n/d' holds only as k->inf; at finite k it is a k-dependent formula, and it only checks the reducer. No null with unplanted target (no root in base) and no generic random bidegree-(2,2) polynomial null; no check that the 2 polys are coprime / that resultant recovers the planted root (Coppersmith multivariate is heuristic, so 'rigorous certificate' is not what the toy can show). (4) 'Provably fails above 1/4' is unsupported for S_3: free-oracle existence count for a planted pair needs 2l<n, i.e. l/n<1/2, and the 1/4..1/6 numbers belong to m=3 (S_4: 1/24 reach vs needed 1/4 per brief). A reduction failing above a bound proves nothing about all algorithms. (5) Scaling: the headline claim covers S_5 (1/80) but only S_3 is tested; S_5 box dims (8k+1)^4 are infeasible, S_4 k=1 is dim 125 (feasible), k=2 dim 729 (marginal). Toy-to-131: lattice dimension is independent of n, so the profile is a function of (k, l/n) plus O(1/n) rounding; extrapolation to n=131 is legitimate if n-independence is demonstrated and n=131 itself is run (cheap). (6) Programme value: this re-derives the existing 'Lattice reach' closure (Z analogue computed by prebuilt lit2026_w10_coppersmith_bound / smallroot_joint_lattice) in a new ring; expected_class theory, cannot lower B*D^2; reach 1/6 is far below the l/n>=1/2 needed for S_3 base to even contain decompositions, and 1/80 vs needed ~0.17-0.25 is a kill, not a lever.
fix: Redesign: (A) Per-(n,k) threshold scan instead of fixed ratios: for n in {31,43,61,97,131} (131 is cheap, 49-dim), k in {1,2,3,4,5} (dims 9..121), sweep every integer l and record l*(n,k)=largest l with >=1 row (and separately >=2 rows) of scaled degree < k*n. Pre-register predictions: first-vector l*/n -> floor-adjusted avg(s)/avg(a+b) = 1/18,1/10,5/42,7/54,0.1364 for k=1..5 (shift set: monomials x1^a x2^b, a,b<=2k, multiplier f^min(a//2,b//2) * P^(k-s)), and compute the 2-vector prediction from the null arm. Statistic: exact integer l* and sorted row-degree profile, not wall time. Check identity sum(rowdeg)=deg det as reducer unit test. (B) Arms: (i) real binary S_3 with x3=x_R random full-degree, a6 random; (ii) generic null: random bidegree-(2,2) polynomial with unit leading coefficient and same support, same modulus; (iii) unplanted vs planted target (profiles must be identical; planted additionally must recover (x1,x2) by resultant/GCD over F_2[t] and the success flag = recovered root equals planted AND >=2 coprime polys). Prediction_if_true: l*(S_3) equals l*(null) equals formula, 0 recoveries above it, recoveries at or below. Prediction_if_false: l*(S_3) > l*(null) (structured extra short vectors) or recovery above formula, or profile differs between planted and unplanted. (C) Univariate control with degree d in {2,3,5}: compare to the exact finite-k formula, not n/d. (D) Add S_4 (3 unknowns, degree 4/var) at k=1 (dim 125) with the same arms; state S_5 k=1 is infeasible (dim 6561) and the 1/80 claim is carried only by the determinant formula, checked as identity. (E) Report as 'finite-k floor-checked determinant identity plus 2nd-vector gap', drop the words 'provably fails' and 'rigorous certificate' (multivariate Coppersmith is heuristic), and state the non-genericity line: cannot move B*D^2, constant/theory-only. Estimated cost with python-int clmul: under 15 CPU-min for n<=131, k<=4; k=5 only for n<=61.
